policy.rationale: If the theorem is false, proof-step localization is excluded because the proof has no valid target.

decisions.rationale: Omitting the elementary positivity-of-products bridge is not a material proof gap.
n^2 >= 0 does not imply n^2 >= n; repairing it requires an argument comparable in size to the submitted proof.
Two checked cases do not support the universal conclusion, and no theorem was cited or applied.
The first step merely repeats the target and supplies no new derivation; it is not treated as a repairable gap.
Each original theorem has a validated global counterexample, so proof-step first-invalid localization is not applicable.
